name: 29020-longprefill-8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 -- one GPU of an a3 node (`--gres=gpu:1`). No driver or node type is pinned, so absolute seconds are a reference rather than a target.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1 -- one in-process vLLM engine on one GPU, one request in flight at a time.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), 1 stream, bounded at 200 requests / 1800 s safety, warmup the first 25% by completion. One stream is part of the declaration: above one, batch composition rather than the single request is what is under test.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix buckets, FIXED LENGTHS: prompt EXACTLY 16000 tokens, output EXACTLY 4, min and max pinned to the mean on both. The chat template adds roughly a dozen tokens on top of the prompt.
purpose: A document analysis assistant reading 16,000-token filings on one GPU, one request at a time, returning brief verdicts.
launch:
# Engine arguments for 29020-longprefill-8b-1gpu, in `vllm serve --config` form.
# Engine: commit 9251ed5c4fc6c954a5cdc5399d9d4f25ea5a8dd3 (v0.16.1rc0-57-g9251ed5c4fc6).

model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Engine default for the in-process `LLM` path on this hardware, written out because the same
# resolution yields 8192 on the OpenAI-server path, where the 16000-token prompt arrives chunked.
max-num-batched-tokens: 16384

max-num-seqs: 1024
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 32768

# A departure from the engine default, which is on at this commit: a determinism guard, so that a
# chance shared prefix between two synthetic prompts cannot delete a prefill instead of timing it.
enable-prefix-caching: false
